text:
Jordan Martinook is 34, in his 800s for games played, and still doing what he has done in Carolina for years: kill penalties and score just often enough to matter. Four goals and 11 points in 23 games puts him on a pace a little above his own range, and the last 10 games (three goals, two assists) have been his best stretch.

The process backs it. The Hurricanes take 62% of the expected goals at five on five when he's out there, and his own chance rate (0.89 expected goals per 60) is above last season's. He has actually scored a goal fewer than his chances deserve, so nothing here looks inflated. The two-goal night in the 9-2 win over Chicago was earned: 0.76 expected goals.

Context matters with him. Evolving-Hockey notes his teammates rank in the 93rd percentile by impact, which flatters raw on-ice numbers, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says he carries the puck in on only 27% of entries, so his line lives on the dump and chase. On a team defending a Stanley Cup, that's a role, and he's filling it well. Our range has him around 36 points.
